record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.original_question: Let G be a group and let M and N be closed aspherical manifolds whose fundamental groups are both isomorphic to G. Must M and N be homeomorphic, and must every homotopy equivalence M -> N be homotopic to a homeomorphism?

evidence.quote: If M and N are aspherical closed manifolds with π1(M) ∼= π1(N) ∼= G, then M and N are homeomorphic and any homotopy equivalence M → N is homotopic to a homeomorphism.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A connected topological space X is called aspherical if its higher homotopy groups vanish, i.e. π_k(X) = 0 for all k ≥ 2 (equivalently, its universal cover is contractible). Let G be a (discrete) group, and let M and N be closed aspherical manifolds (compact, without boundary, topological manifolds) whose fundamental groups satisfy π_1(M) ≅ G ≅ π_1(N). Determine whether the following two statements always hold:

(a) M and N are homeomorphic.
(b) Every homotopy equivalence f : M → N is homotopic to a homeomorphism.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Borel Conjecture, one of the central open problems in geometric topology. It has been established in many special cases (e.g. by Farrell–Jones for manifolds whose fundamental groups are word-hyperbolic or CAT(0), and in low dimensions), but the general conjecture remains open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Borel conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Borel conjecture asserts that closed aspherical manifolds with isomorphic fundamental groups are homeomorphic, and any homotopy equivalence is homotopic to a homeomorphism. The conjecture remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: The Borel Conjecture is a well-known open conjecture in topology.

status_evidence.title: Bartels–Lück: The Borel conjecture for hyperbolic and CAT(0)-groups
status_evidence.snippet: Bartels and Lück proved the Borel conjecture for groups that are hyperbolic or CAT(0), confirming many cases but leaving the general statement open.
status_evidence.claim: Major cases are resolved (Farrell–Jones program, Bartels–Lück), but the general Borel conjecture is still open.
